races.title: State House, District 34
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Tim Longest
cands.bio: Democratic member of the North Carolina House for District 34 since January 2023. Lawyer with a UNC-Chapel Hill bachelor's degree (2013) and a UNC School of Law degree (2018). Says he has worked in all three branches of state government.

endorsements.text: Sierra Club North Carolina is listed among his 2026 endorsements and voter guide recommendations.

cands.gaps: We found no documented statements or actions from Longest on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, immigration enforcement or H-1B, policing and public-order measures, or gun laws. His only first-person policy statements come from a 2022 candidate survey. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2024 or 2026 surveys. The pages we had list no sponsored bills, so we could not show specific deeds. His upbringing is described differently in two sources (see for_review). We found no controversies, foreign ties or notable endorsements beyond the Sierra Club North Carolina listing.

local.label: Roots 100: Ballotpedia and Wikipedia say he was born in Greenville, NC, and Wikipedia says he was raised in Elizabeth City. He calls himself an Eastern North Carolina native and a product of NC public schools from kindergarten through law school.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Lawyer and North Carolina House member since January 2023, with service on the Finance committee among others. He says he has worked in all three branches of state government.
qual.why: He has prior legislative service of about three years plus a law career, which fits the high band for writing law and budgets. His earlier work in each branch of government is self-reported, so the score stops short of the top of the range.
qual.label: He has prior legislative service of about three years plus a law career, which fits the high band for writing law and budgets. His earlier work in each branch of government is self-reported, so the score stops short of the top of the range.

pro-life.evidence: In a 2022 Ballotpedia survey he said he is "proudly pro-choice," that abortion is a private decision between a woman and her doctor, and that he would fight any new abortion restrictions.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: In a 2022 Ballotpedia survey he said he supports raising teacher pay above the national average. He also said he would restore funding to public schools. He did not address vouchers or charters in that survey, and he did not give a 25% figure.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: In a 2022 Ballotpedia survey he said he would fight to protect air and water, green spaces and wildlife. He gave no specific growth or zoning policy.

prio.label: Matches 2 of 3 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 2 only promised

cands.name: Ed George
cands.bio: Libertarian candidate for North Carolina House District 34 in 2024 and 2026, losing to Democratic incumbent Tim Longest both times. His campaign site says he studied engineering and now leads large industrial construction projects in North Carolina. He has held no elected office.
cands.gaps: We could not find where Ed George was born, which Appalachian state he grew up in, or when he moved to North Carolina. His campaign site says he bought a condo in the district nine years before the page was written, but gives no date. We found no record of elected office, bills or official actions. His site does not state positions on data centers, property taxes, development, land ownership, immigration, policing, guns or abortion. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2024 or 2026, and Ballotpedia lists no endorsements for him. Details of his construction career, such as employer and projects, come only from his own site and were not independently confirmed.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.why: A career managing large projects fits the middle band (managers and business backgrounds). He has no prior legislative service or policy or budget work, and the career details are self-reported.
